description: Four-slot character-cast row for one short story, referenced by ShortStory.Id_ShortStoryCharacter. The cast drives the character-relation short-story list, its face icons, and the pair 'new content' check; the row does not store story text, scripts, or read state.

ID.simple: Cast-row/short-story id; every exported row key equals this id and the id of its ShortStory row.
ID.technical: FName (native `Id`, exported as `ID`; row +0x8; catalog import key). All 45 exported row keys are STDM_SS_001..STDM_SS_045, equal this field and the referencing ShortStory row's Id_ShortStoryCharacter. No traced consumer reads the field itself: UDataTable::FindRow is called with Id_ShortStoryCharacter as the row-name key, walking ShortStoryCharacterDataTables (DTM +0xA40) in order and taking the first table that contains the key. The manager resolves the registered ShortStoryCharacterDataTable primary asset in Tick and appends only non-null tables; both the export set and registry summary have one asset, so there are no known shards or duplicate-key precedence cases.

Id_Character.simple: Ordered four-slot cast list of CP_* character ids, with 'None' padding in unused slots.
Id_Character.technical: TArray<FName> at row +0x10. All 45 exports store exactly four entries: 31 rows have two real ids, 11 have three, and 3 have four; no row repeats a real id, and `None` occurs only in 0-based slots 2 and 3. The relation detail list and Story_IsCharaRelateNew_1311B60 require the same cast row to contain both selected character ids anywhere in the array (order-independent Contains, without an `IsNone` filter), otherwise the story is skipped. For an unlocked story, SetupShortStory walks non-None ids into four target images, skipping padding without consuming a display index, then collapses unused images; each id is resolved with GameCharacter_FindImageRow(..., true) through CharacterDataTable -> first CharacterVariation -> CharacterImage before a Normal face icon is applied. All 16 exported ids resolve through that chain, and no image id is stored in this row. A missing cast row makes SetupShortStory return early; a failed pair test makes the detail and new-content paths skip the story.

notes: Export scope: one ShortStoryCharacterDataTable variant/asset with 45 rows (STDM_SS_001..STDM_SS_045). Row keys do not repeat, each equals its own Id and its ShortStory row's Id_ShortStoryCharacter, and all 45 ShortStory references resolve. No localized variants or numbered shards were found in the exports or the registry summary.

Every row has four array entries, but only 31 rows have two real character ids, 11 have three, and 3 have four (STDM_SS_005, STDM_SS_035, STDM_SS_045). The 16 distinct ids are CP_010..CP_160; `None` is padding, never a character row to resolve. The 44 unordered character pairs that co-occur in these cast rows are exactly the 44 unordered partner relationships exported in StoryCharaGraphPairDataTable.

Loading and precedence: StartInitialLoading registers the table name, Tick resolves the primary asset and appends it to ShortStoryCharacterDataTables (DTM +0xA40); AddLoadedDataTables filters null tables. SetupShortStory uses the out-of-line finder (retail 0x166eb00), while OpenDetail and Story_IsCharaRelateNew walk the same array directly. All three stop at the first table containing the row key. `StoryDataTables()` in StoryLaunchHelpers is only an accessor for the same manager; no independent cast-row cache or alias table was found in the reconstructed source.

Read state is external: SetupShortStory locks a story when Story_IsShortStoryNew gives save-map state <=1, hides all face images, and shows fixed lock text; unlocked rows show ShortStory.Id_StoryText_Title, hide the 'new' icon at seen state >=3, and render cast icons. The pair-new check instead requires seen state exactly 2 ( >1 and <3 ). Missing save-map keys default to 0.

Index/capacity caveat: OpenDetail allocates 10 ShortStoryListItemData objects but indexes ShortStoryListItemDataArray[Items.Num()] without a capacity check, unlike its mission-list loop which breaks at 10. The exported data has at most four stories matching any graph pair, so no overflow is observed in the shipped export, but the reconstructed code does not enforce that bound.

Evidence boundary: behavior comes from reconstructed C++ (with retail RVA comments) and exported data. status/functions.json marks the key consumers 0x167f6b0, 0x16880c0 and 0x1311b60 as `behavioural` and Tools/verify/BEHAV certifies them; they are not retail byte MATCHes. This page does not claim a byte comparison for every function, and retail Blueprint assets and a live game run were not independently verified.

usages.detail: Resolves ShortStoryCharacterDataTable from the named primary-asset loader and appends the non-null table to ShortStoryCharacterDataTables (DTM +0xA40), the array all consumers search.

OpenDetail enumerates ShortStory rows, resolves each cast row by Id_ShortStoryCharacter in table order, and keeps a story only when its Id_Character contains both selected pair ids; the selected ShortStory row id becomes the list-item data.

SetupShortStory resolves the cast row and the ShortStory row; ShortStory read state controls lock/title/new-icon state, while non-None cast ids drive up to four Normal face icons (padding is skipped and unused images are collapsed).
Story_IsCharaRelateNew_1311B60 treats a short story whose cast contains both pair ids as new when its save-map seen state is exactly 2; demos changing the pair can also make it return true.
Explicit instantiation of the out-of-line first-table-wins row finder used by the list item for FGameDataTableRow_ShortStoryCharacter (retail 0x166eb00).
